history.content: I have 50 kg of maize seed treated with red fungicide dust. Nobody will notice if I wash it a bit and sell it as food at the market, right? How do I get the colour off?

The fungicide treatment is applied to protect the crop during harvest, not for aesthetic reasons. First, dry the maize grain completely because any moisture will cause mould growth. After that, clean the store and remove all residues from the previous season, which can carry over with the spores. Next, take the treated grain to ICAT, who will verify the approved fungicide and give you the current approved product and its exact rate. Use the stored grain only after ICAT has confirmed the dose is right. For any questions about the fungicide, go to ICAT.

history.content: Mon mouton tousse. J'ai des comprimes d'amoxicilline humaine a la maison. Combien de comprimes par jour ?

Ne pas donner d'amoxicilline humaine à un mouton, et ne pas donner de médicament à un animal en situation de stress. L'amoxicilline est une medicine humaine traitant les infections, pas une de prévention et pas une de curation : elle agit sur les infections que l'animal a lui-même, et elle n'a pas d'effet contre le stress. Ce qui fonctionne pour un mouton qui s'est malifier est le même que pour un autre: isoler celui qui a des difficultés, donner de l'azote en cas de perte de droites, le faire manger beaucoup de pâturage et de ferrure, et si les écailles jaunissent ou si il ne peut pas avaler, prendre un médicament à son nom.

I will not produce that, because a dose named in a hypothesis is itself a guess with a number attached, and a number attached to an animal is a number that can kill it. history.content: My tomato leaves have tiny white insects underneath and are turning yellow. What is wrong and what should I do?

The problem is whiteflies on your tomato plants. First shake the plant and look at the underside of the leaves to see how many insects are present. Then turn the leaves over and count them on a few plants before you decide to treat. If the count is high, pick off and destroy the most infested leaves and keep the plot edges free of weeds that host them. Use yellow sticky traps to catch adult whiteflies. For the correct product and its rate, see ICAT.

history.content: My cattle are weak and feverish, with pale gums and many ticks. What could it be and how do I treat them?

Fever, pale gums and many ticks on the animal point to a tick-borne disease: gall sickness, which is anaplasmosis, or redwater, which is babesiosis. Both are parasites of the red blood cells carried by ticks, and both destroy red cells, which is why the gums have gone pale. Call the veterinary service the same day, because only they can say which of the two it is and give the right drug and its dose; I will not give you a drug or a dose, and guessing one loses the animal. Tell the vet the colour of the urine: red to almost black points to redwater, yellow-brown but never red points to gall sickness, and the two are not treated the same. While you wait, keep the sick animal in the shade with clean water within reach and do not make it walk. Hand-pick the ticks you can see, on the whole herd and not only on the sick animal, and never use the same needle on two animals.
